NodeInfo.Pods() returns pods scheduled and assumed, FilteredList only has pods scheduled.
If a pod is assumed to a node, but failed finally, will it break the affinity predicate?

> NodeInfo.Pods() returns pods scheduled and assumed, FilteredList only has pods scheduled.
> If a pod is assumed to a node, but failed finally, will it break the affinity predicate?

It seems predicate metadata also did not consider the assumed pod.

When considering the anti-affinity, I think we should use nodeInfo(scheduled and assumed) ranther than podlister (only scheduled) .
Two reason
1 speed up
2 if the assumed pod is finally scheduled to the node, but we don’t consider it, it may break anti-affinity predicate 
 

When considering the affinity, I think we should only consider the scheduled pod. Here, I think we should and scheduledPods for nodeInfo.  In the cluster with lots of pods, we use podLister which will costs lots of time.

Yes.

The else block (nil/fail metadata case) was designed in particular for non-default algorithm provider, which IMO is intentionally using lister.Pods(). @bsalamat please confirm if it's autoscaler provider's intention.

Maybe you're talking about the issue that nil node can cause the metadata to be nil? That's a bug definitely and is already fixed by tolerating the nil node when generating metadata, so that case won't hit the else block again.

Generally speaking, for a default algorithm provider, if the metadata comes to nil, we should consider it as a bug and fix in the right place. And non-default algorithm provider is the only case to hit the else block.

> and fix in the right place. And non-default algorithm provider is the only case to hit the else

+1, we should not merge the change in this PR. This is a special code path that if executed in the standard scheduler indicates a bug. One example external entity that uses our code and exercise this code path is [cluster autoscaler](https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/blob/0e17b313a43fc554c0ea56f7f3de5213a46a8156/cluster-autoscaler/core/utils.go#L222), they also build the NodeInfo object in their code, so it is sadly their decision how to optimize this code path.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/955198751cdbf10701607490937d35d0e3d57e50/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/predicates/predicates.go#L1351

why we don't just use the function nodeInfo.Pods() to get the pods' info?

review_comments:
For satisfiesExistingPodsAntiAffinity func, it just check whether the pod schedule onto this node would break any anti-affinity terms by the existing pod on the node. So here can just get the affinity pods on the node.

```
filteredPods := nodeInfo.PodsWithAffinity()
```
filteredPods := nodeInfo.Pods() can be applied to satisfiesPodsAffinityAntiAffinity func,
We shouldn't do that because the existing pod without any affinity may be anti-affinity with the pod we are scheduling.

> We shouldn't do that because the existing pod without any affinity may be anti-affinity with the pod we are scheduling.

nodeInfo.PodsWithAffinity() include the pods that have podAffinity or podAntiAffinity.

> So here can just get the affinity pods on the node.
> filteredPods := nodeInfo.PodsWithAffinity()

> filteredPods := nodeInfo.Pods() can be applied to satisfiesPodsAffinityAntiAffinity func,

Sorry, I'm confused, what are you suggesting?

> > So here can just get the affinity pods on the node.
> > filteredPods := nodeInfo.PodsWithAffinity()
> 
> > filteredPods := nodeInfo.Pods() can be applied to satisfiesPodsAffinityAntiAffinity func,
> 
> Sorry, I'm confused, what are you suggesting?

For satisfiesExistingPodsAntiAffinity func, it just check whether the incoming pod schedule onto this node would break any anti-affinity terms by the existing pod on the node. It will use the incoming pod's namespace and label to match the existing pod's anti-affinity term on the node. 
And the nodeInfo already has all pods with affinity. So we can use it directly.
```
filteredPods := nodeInfo.PodsWithAffinity()
```

And in satisfiesPodsAffinityAntiAffinity func, it will check the incoming pod's affinity/anti-affinity terms whether match the pod's label and namespace. The nodeInfo did not have pods with namespaces.

> > So here can just get the affinity pods on the node.
> > filteredPods := nodeInfo.PodsWithAffinity()
> 
> > filteredPods := nodeInfo.Pods() can be applied to satisfiesPodsAffinityAntiAffinity func,
> 
> Sorry, I'm confused, what are you suggesting?

The suggestion maybe need to consider the assumed pods.
